AiEnablement.description:
Which AI surfaces are enabled. Every field defaults to **off**: a
deployment that upgrades into a build containing AI code gets no AI
behaviour, no model traffic, and no GPU expectation until someone turns it
on deliberately. This is the same ships-dark posture `idempotency` and
`approval` already use, and it is the correct default for a subsystem whose
failure modes include "said something wrong to a customer".
`Default` is derived rather than hand-written specifically so that adding a
new surface field cannot accidentally default it to `true` — the derive
gives every `bool` `false`, which is the ships-dark answer, and there is no
hand-maintained list to forget to update.

enabled.description:
Master switch. `false` disables **every** AI surface regardless of the
per-surface flags below — an operator reaching for the kill-switch
during an incident must not have to reason about which of five flags
they missed.

fields.description:
AI form fields and components (`MODULE_AI`) — summarise, draft,
classify, translate. Read-only suggestions.

semantic_search.description:
Semantic/dense retrieval within search (`MODULE_SEARCH`). Turning this
off leaves lexical search fully working — that degradation is a
supported configuration, not an outage (P-inference §4.3).

AnchorStoreSection.description:
The dedicated, WORM-provisioned bucket external audit anchors are written
to, and the **append-only** credential they are written with — D-352,
closing the gap `xrm_audit::anchor`'s module doc has named since D-174.

**Why this is a second bucket and not `storage`.** D-174 anchored to the
deployment's general object store, reusing `storage`'s client and
credential. That cannot be made immutable: the same credential must keep
`DeleteObject` for the upload paths that genuinely delete objects
(`xrm_document::files::…`, `files_scan`'s quarantine cleanup and rejected-scan
purge), and Object Lock retention on that bucket would break every one of
them. An anchor whose own writer can delete it is not an independent
record of anything — a party who compromised the deployment holds that
credential. So the anchor bucket is separate, its producer credential
carries `PutObject`/`GetObject`/`ListBucket` and nothing else, and
delete/retention authority lives with an operator identity that is never
stored on the deployment host. See `deploy/audit-anchor/README.md`.

**What this struct can and cannot enforce.** Object Lock is provisioned on
the bucket, out-of-band, before the deployment ever starts — application
code cannot turn it on, and nothing here pretends otherwise. The two
`object_lock_*` fields are an operator *declaration* of what was
provisioned, and `validate_production_profile` refuses to boot a production
deployment that has anchoring on without them. A declaration is not proof,
which is why it is deliberately not the only control: `preflight` probes
the credential's append-only-ness live, and
`scripts/audit/anchor-immutability-drill.sh` proves the retention half
against the real bucket. The boot check's job is to make "we forgot to
provision it" a loud failure rather than a silent one.

object_lock_mode.description:
What the operator provisioned on the bucket, out-of-band:
`"compliance"`, `"governance"`, or `"none"`. Mirrors
`deploy/backup/README.md`'s fallback ladder, and means the same things:
compliance mode cannot be bypassed even by the bucket owner's root
credentials; governance mode can, by a distinct identity holding
`s3:BypassGovernanceRetention`. `"none"` is honest about having no
bucket-side backstop at all and is refused in production.

object_lock_retention_days.description:
The default retention period, in days, configured on the bucket. Must
be at least as long as the deployment's audit-retention obligation —
an anchor that expires before the events it attests to is worse than
useless, because the chain then looks anchored right up until the
moment someone needs it. Zero is refused in production.

s3_access_key.description:
The **producer** identity: `PutObject`/`GetObject`/`ListBucket` only.
No `DeleteObject`, no `DeleteObjectVersion`, no
`PutBucketVersioning`/`PutBucketPolicy`/`PutLifecycleConfiguration`, no
`s3:BypassGovernanceRetention`, no `PutObjectRetention` (which would
let a compromised app shorten its own retention).

s3_bucket.description:
Must differ from `storage.s3_bucket` — `validate()` rejects the same
bucket for both, since the whole point is that this one is WORM and
that one cannot be.

s3_endpoint.description:
S3-compatible endpoint holding the anchor bucket. May be the same
endpoint as `storage.s3_endpoint` (one RustFS/MinIO deployment, two
buckets) or a wholly separate one — a different account, region, or
provider is strictly better, since it widens the blast-radius gap this
whole mechanism exists to create. Empty selects AWS S3 proper (the
same convention `storage.s3_endpoint` uses).

contract_reference.description:
U11-T1: the operator's contract or purchase-order reference, shown on
the usage page. Free text; nothing is enforced by it.

debug_pipeline_trace.description:
Z5-T1: in a debug build, every response carries `x-attome-layers`,
the layers the request passed, outermost first, so a test can pin
the middleware order. Ignored in a release build.

deployment_profile.description:
P-production-safety-profile — one of `"development"`/`"production"`
(see `VALID_DEPLOYMENT_PROFILES` in `validate()`). Default
`"development"` — today's behavior, unchanged: every other field in
this file keeps whatever value an operator gave it, validated only by
the per-field checks that already existed. Setting `"production"` is
an explicit, additional opt-in (never derived from `APP_ENV`, which
already means "tolerate unresolved `${VAR}` placeholders for local
dev" — a different concern) that runs `validate_production_profile`:
a fixed set of individually-valid-but-unsafe-in-combination defaults
(`database.ssl_mode = "prefer"`, `cache.tls_enabled = false`,
`storage.s3_verify_ssl = false`,
no `auth.apikey_default_expiry_days`,
`audit.signing_enabled = false`, `database.migrate_on_boot = true`,
`jobs.run_worker_inline = true`) become hard boot errors instead of
silent template carry-overs. No per-check escape hatch by design — a
hatch on any one of these would reopen exactly the gap this profile
closes.

Not the *only* thing gated on this field: `validate_production_profile`
below is `attome-config`'s own complete list, but `server::boot::init`
(the composition root, which has visibility this crate doesn't) reads
this same value too — D-327's `idempotency.mandatory_operations`
completeness floor is production-only for exactly the same reason,
just enforced one layer up. Don't assume this field's production
requirements begin and end with what's checked in this file.

failover_retry_max_secs.description:
AB2-T3: seconds a GET, HEAD or `Idempotency-Key` request that lost its
database connection is run again inside the server, across a failover.
0 turns it off; at most 30.

max_concurrent_per_ip.description:
Z5-T5: requests one address runs at once before answering 429 with
`Retry-After: 1`. 1 to `max_concurrent_requests`.

max_concurrent_requests.description:
Z5-T5: requests this node runs at once before answering 503 with
`Retry-After: 1`, ahead of authentication. 1 to 1,000,000.

packs.description:
Packs applied at every boot, in order (`attome init --pack crm`): each
pack's changesets from `<packs_root>/<name>/changesets/`, through the
changeset ledger, so a second boot changes nothing.

packs_root.description: Where packs live. Unset: `packs` next to the executable.

public_frontend_url.description:
P-account-lifecycle — canonical public URL used to build links in
emails (password reset, verification), e.g. "https://app.customer.com".
`None` (the default) falls back to the same dev-only derived origin
`allowed_origins()` uses (`http://{frontend_host}:{frontend_port}`) —
any deployment behind TLS must set this explicitly, mirroring the
`cors.allowed_origins` rule.

shutdown_drain_delay_secs.description:
S1 (BSV-F13 / BSV-D11) — how many seconds a draining node keeps
answering `/health/ready` with 503 **before** it signals its HTTP
listeners to stop accepting connections.

`main.rs` flips `AppState::draining` and then waits this long; without
it the flag and the graceful-shutdown signal fire in the same instant,
axum stops `accept()` immediately, and the only way a load balancer
could ever read the 503 was an already-open keep-alive connection — the
probe it actually makes opens a new one and gets connection refused. One
LB probe interval x failure threshold is the right value; `0` restores
the pre-S1 behaviour (flip and signal in the same tick).

D-205-safe default: hand-written `default_shutdown_drain_delay_secs`
returns 10, not a derived `Default`'s 0 (which would silently disable
the drain the moment the key is omitted). `AppSection` itself is not
`#[serde(default)]` in `AppConfig` (its `frontend_host`/`port` are
required), so an omitted `app` block already fails to deserialize and
this default can only apply to an omitted key inside a present block.
Bounded to `0..=SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_DELAY_MAX_SECS` by
`AppConfig::validate`.

time_zone.description:
A4-T1: the deployment's time zone, an IANA name such as `Asia/Riyadh`.
Dates in autonumber formats and their yearly, monthly and daily resets
follow it. Unset (or unknown): UTC.

tls.description:
Z5-T6: the server terminates TLS itself (HTTP/2 and HTTP/1.1), so a
single server needs no reverse proxy in front of it.

web_root.description:
The built web app's directory, served by `attome serve` for every
GET outside the API (`attome_server::web`). Unset: a `web` directory
next to the executable when one exists; otherwise the server serves
the API only and the web app is hosted separately.

required_actions.description:
`action_type` strings (e.g. `"security.rewrap"`,
`"security.role_grant"`; `xrm_server::KNOWN_ACTION_TYPES` is the list
of record) that must go
through `attome_approval::submit` instead of executing inline. Empty
by default — a deployment opts in explicitly, same shape as
`idempotency.mandatory_operations`.

Validated at boot, not here (same shape as
`IdempotencySection::mandatory_operations`): `server::boot::init`'s
`validate_operation_registries` checks every entry here against
`xrm_server::KNOWN_ACTION_TYPES` (mirroring `execute_approved`'s
match arms) and fails the boot closed on an unrecognized action_type,
instead of silently never gating anything. `attome-config` still has no
visibility into this itself (guidelines §1: base-* has zero xrm-*
knowledge) — the composition root owns the check.

ttl_hours.description:
How long a submitted request stays decidable before
`attome_approval::sweep_expired` reaps it as `expired`.

anchor_store.description:
D-352 (TODO-004 / review finding H-1) — the dedicated WORM bucket and
append-only credential anchors are written with. See
[`AnchorStoreSection`] for why this is not `storage`.

`None` (the default) keeps D-174's original behavior: anchors go to
this deployment's general `storage` bucket with the app's own
credential, which is tamper-*evident* (nothing overwrites an anchor
through this application, `PutMode::Create`) but not tamper-*proof*
(that credential can delete through the storage backend directly).
That remains fine for development. `validate_production_profile`
refuses it in production whenever `external_anchoring_enabled` is
true — a production deployment claiming external anchoring while the
anchor's own writer can delete it is the finding this closes.

chainer_enabled.description:
P1.13 stage 4 — the cutover, and since D-316 the **default**. When
true, `write()` only durably captures the event into
`xrm_audit_ingest` (no lock, no chain read) and the `audit_chainer`
process becomes solely responsible for producing header rows —
requires `audit_chainer` to actually be running, or events accumulate
in `xrm_audit_ingest` unchained (the lag gauge, the
`AuditChainerLagHigh` alert, and finally `ingest_backlog_threshold`'s
mutation gate are what make that visible rather than silent).

False keeps the pre-P1.13 synchronous path: `AuditService::write`
acquires the per-organization append lock and writes
`xrm_audit_header`/`detail`/`snapshot` inline, inside the caller's
business transaction. That path serializes **every** mutation in the
deployment on one lock (D-002: one organization, one chain), which
the 2026-08-10 engineering review reproduced as ordinary concurrent
saves failing with `Conflict` after the 200 × 5 ms retry budget
(F-001), each retry sleeping with an open transaction holding a
pooled connection (F-010). It is therefore supported only for
single-writer development — `validate_production_profile` refuses to
boot a `production` deployment with it false (D-316).

To roll back a deployment to the sync path: flip this to false, and
run `audit_chainer` once more afterwards to drain whatever was
captured while it was on (the chainer deliberately still starts with
this false, exactly so that drain step is possible — see its module
doc).

erasure_enabled.description:
D-107 (P-data-lifecycle item (d)'s erasure ruling) — crypto-shredding.
When active, every audit write for a record with an `id`
fetches-or-creates that record's data-encryption key
(`xrm_audit_erasure_key`, migration 0039) and encrypts its field values
in place before any storage — see `xrm_audit::erasure`.

D-540 (G2-2 a): optional. Omitted means "on wherever a key is
configured" — active exactly when `erasure_key_encryption_key` is
non-empty ([`AuditSection::erasure_active`]). An explicit `false` keeps
it off and stays allowed outside production; an explicit `true` without
a key is a boot error. `validate_production_profile` refuses a
`production` deployment unless it is active with a real key (D-540
ruling 1, audit plan item 2.7).

erasure_key_encryption_key.description:
D-107 — AES-256-GCM master key(s) (64 hex chars each) wrapping every
record's data-encryption key in `xrm_audit_erasure_key.wrapped_dek`. A
*dedicated* key, same reasoning as `auth.mfa_encryption_key` not
reusing `s2s.key_encryption_key`: audit-erasure keys are their own
trust domain. Only required (`check_secret`-validated) when
`erasure_enabled = true`. Generate with: openssl rand -hex 32.
P-key-rotation-and-jwt (a): a `KeyRing` — see that type's doc.

external_anchoring_enabled.description:
P-audit-chain-hardening item (b) — anchors each sealed batch's
Merkle root to the deployment's own configured object store
(`attome_storage`, e.g. RustFS), outside this database's own blast
radius, so a compromise of the DB+app config together can no longer
silently rewrite history undetected. Default false: ships dark, same
posture as every other flag in this section. Best-effort — an
anchoring failure is logged/alertable but never blocks the chainer's
own batch commit (`xrm_audit::chainer`'s degrade-not-fail design,
D-027). See `xrm_audit::anchor`.

ingest_backlog_threshold.description:
P-audit-chain-hardening item (e) — ingest circuit breaker. How many
undrained `xrm_audit_ingest` rows (summed across organizations,
`xrm_audit::chainer::aggregate_lag`'s `total_pending_ingest`) trip
the mutating-request gate (`AppState::audit_ingest_backlog_exceeded`).
100_000 matches the originating review's own number — a starting
point, not a measured one; tune per deployment. Reads are never
affected, only `POST`/`PUT`/`PATCH`/`DELETE`.

ingest_capture_enabled.description:
P1.13 stage 1: additionally durably capture every audit event into
`xrm_audit_ingest` (same transaction as the existing header/detail/
snapshot writes) so a future async chainer has something to drain.
Purely additive today — the synchronous chain append in
`AuditService::write` still runs unconditionally either way; this
flag does not yet turn it off. Default false until the chainer
(a later P1.13 stage) exists to consume the table.

ingest_retention_days.description:
P1.13 step 6 — how many days a `xrm_audit_ingest` row is kept after
its batch has already been drained into `xrm_audit_header` (i.e. it
is provably redundant, kept only for a debugging/replay window).
`0` disables pruning entirely — an explicit opt-in, never a
default-on delete of audit data.

Audit 10/10 plan item 2.8: only ingest ranges whose chain batches are
signed and externally anchored are pruned, and the pruned watermark is
recorded so verification still passes. With
`external_anchoring_enabled = false` nothing is pruned, whatever this
is set to (`xrm_audit::chainer::prune_ingest`).

partition_create_ahead_months.description:
P-db-maintenance item (c) — how many months of partitions the
create-ahead job keeps provisioned beyond the current one, for the
audit family + `xrm_s2s_access_log` (migrations/0026). `2` matches
the plan's stated default; raise it for a deployment whose
maintenance window runs less often than this job's own poll interval.

signing_enabled.description:
Sign every audit chain event's (prev_hash||event_hash) with a
dedicated Ed25519 keypair (D-016 — unrelated to the license
verifier's verify-only key in xrm-license, D-142). When false,
`signature`/`signing_key_id` are left NULL; hash-chaining alone
still applies.

signing_key_id.description:
Identifies which keypair produced a signature — stays alongside every
signature it makes so old signatures remain attributable after a key
rotation. Any operator-chosen label, e.g. "audit-key-1".

signing_private_key.description:
64-hex-char Ed25519 signing seed. Required when signing_enabled = true.
Generate with: openssl rand -hex 32

access_token_expiry_mins.description:
Access-token (session_token cookie) lifetime, in minutes. Deliberately
short (Plan 1.6a) — the refresh flow is what makes that tolerable.

apikey_default_expiry_days.description:
P-account-lifecycle — default `api_key.expires_at` for newly
created keys, in days. `None` (the default) means new keys still get
no expiry unless the caller passes one explicitly — existing
deployments are unaffected until an operator opts in.

apikey_hash_pepper.description:
P-api-key-hashing (D-112, revised by D-118) — HMAC-SHA256 pepper ring
for `api_key.secret_hash`, superseding per-request Argon2 for
api-key secrets only (user passwords stay Argon2, `password.rs`,
untouched). The *current* pepper — every newly issued key and every
rehash-on-use conversion writes with this one. Unconditionally
`check_secret`-validated in `validate()` below — unlike
`mfa_encryption_key`/`s2s.key_encryption_key`, there is no feature flag
gating this: every deployment authenticates api-key requests, so an
unset/short pepper is always a boot error (D-038), never a silent
unkeyed-hash fallback. `#[serde(default)]` (empty string) only so a
config file that omits it still deserializes — `validate()` is what
actually enforces the requirement.

apikey_hash_pepper_id.description:
Id of `apikey_hash_pepper` above, stored inline in
`api_key.secret_hash` as `hmac256:v{id}$<hex>`. **The very first
pepper a deployment ever sets must use id 0** — id 0 doubles as the
fallback for the original, pre-rotation D-112 rollout's unversioned
`hmac256$<hex>` rows (see `attome_auth::apikey_hash`'s module doc), so a
deployment that skips straight to id 1+ on its very first boot with no
`hmac256$`-format rows in the database is fine, but one migrating
forward from the original rollout MUST keep id 0 resolvable (either
`apikey_hash_pepper_id = 0` or an `apikey_hash_previous_peppers` entry
with `id = 0`) or its existing keys stop verifying. `validate()` below
only enforces the id-collision/duplicate checks it can prove
statically — it cannot know whether unversioned rows exist in a given
database, so this precondition is operator-enforced, documented here
and in D-112's revision entry, not boot-checked.

apikey_hash_previous_peppers.description:
Retired pepper(s), keyed by id, kept only long enough to verify
already-issued keys that haven't rehashed to the current id yet —
same "current + previous" dual-key-slot shape `s2s.key_encryption_key`
already uses for the same reason. Empty (the default) means no
rotation has ever happened. A row referencing an id present in
neither this list nor `apikey_hash_pepper_id` fails closed (same
"wrong secret" outcome as any other verify failure) rather than
erroring — do not remove an id from this list while any
`api_key` row might still reference it.

breach_check_online.description:
Z4-T9: also ask an online k-anonymity range service when a password
is set at registration or reset (off by default; only the first five
hex characters of the password's SHA-1 are sent).

breach_list_file.description:
Q7-T1: an offline set of breached passwords (the Have I Been Pwned
SHA-1 download, `HASH` or `HASH:COUNT` per line), checked locally
when a password is set. Unset, only the small built-in list applies.
Replace the file and restart to update it.

breach_range_url.description:
Z4-T9: the range service, the five-character prefix appended (Have I
Been Pwned's when unset).

geoip_database.description:
Q9-T1: an offline country database in the MaxMind DB format (`.mmdb`:
GeoLite2-Country, DB-IP or IPinfo country files), read by the sign-in
country rules of roles. Unset, a role with a country rule refuses every
sign-in. A file that cannot be read stops boot. Replace the file and
restart to update it.

jwt_audience.description:
P-key-rotation-and-jwt (c) — the `aud` claim every session/pending
token carries and is validated against. Empty (the default) means
"use `jwt_issuer`" (`AppConfig::jwt_audience`) — a deployment only
needs to set this explicitly if it wants a distinct audience string.

jwt_secret.description:
P-key-rotation-and-jwt (a)/(c): a `KeyRing` rather than a bare secret —
see that type's doc. A plain config-file string still deserializes
(wrapped into a single active/legacy entry), so an existing deployment
that never touches this field sees zero behavior change. `kid` in
every minted JWT's header names which ring entry signed it; a second
(retired) entry left in the ring is accepted for verification during a
rotation's overlap window and rejected once removed.

jwt_signing_keys.description:
Z4-T3: Ed25519 signing keys for session and pending tokens, each a
32-byte seed as 64 hex characters, by key id. When the ring has an
active key, new tokens are signed EdDSA under it; `jwt_secret` keeps
verifying the HS256 tokens already issued until they expire, so the
cut-over logs nobody out. Empty (the default) keeps HS256.

kdf.description:
attome-auth plan BAU-15a (hardening 2.7) — the KDF executor and password
policy, formerly constants in `attome_auth::password`. Defaults equal
those constants, so a config without the block behaves as before.
Floors and ceilings are enforced by `AppConfig::validate`.

mfa_challenge_max_attempts.description:
P-mfa-challenge-hardening: per-challenge attempt ceiling enforced
atomically against the `mfa:pending:{jti}` Redis marker (see
`attome_auth::mfa`) — reaching it kills the challenge outright (the
client must re-authenticate with the password for a fresh
`pending_token`), independent of the general per-IP/user
`rate_limit.categories.mfa` budget. Default `5`, same "additive,
default-safe" posture as every other new config field in this
section — a deployment that never touches this sees a sane default,
not a behavior change requiring opt-in.

mfa_encryption_key.description:
P2.8 step 7 — AES-256-GCM master key(s) (64 hex chars each) encrypting
`base_user_mfa.secret_encrypted` at rest, same pattern as
`s2s.key_encryption_key` (`xrm_s2s::crypto`) but a dedicated key: TOTP
secrets and S2S client secrets are separate trust domains and must
not share a key. Only required (`check_secret`-validated) when
`mfa_policy != "off"`. P-key-rotation-and-jwt (a): a `KeyRing` — see
that type's doc for the bare-string back-compat shape and how
rotation works.

mfa_policy.description:
P2.8 step 7 — one of `"off"`/`"optional"`/`"required"` (see
`VALID_MFA_POLICIES` in `validate()`). `"off"` (the default) is
today's behavior unchanged. `"optional"` challenges only accounts
that have self-enrolled TOTP; `"required"` blocks a password login
for an unenrolled account until it completes enrollment
(`attome_auth::mfa`/D-068). Same string-enum convention as
`database.ssl_mode` — deliberately a plain `String`, not a Rust enum.

refresh_absolute_lifetime_days.description:
D-504 — absolute lifetime of a refresh family, in days. A family ends
this long after the credential verification that started it, however
often it rotates. Default 30. `AppConfig::validate` requires 1 to 365;
migration 0462's fallback anchor for an inconsistent lineage relies on
that ceiling to be expired.

refresh_token_expiry_days.description:
Idle lifetime of one `base_refresh_token` row, in days: how long a
refresh token stays valid without being rotated.

registration_mode.description:
P-registration-gating — one of `"public"`/`"invite"`/`"disabled"` (see
`VALID_REGISTRATION_MODES` in `validate()`). Default `"disabled"` —
deliberately secure-by-default (D-128): a deployment upgrading without
touching config loses public self-registration, not the other way
around. `"public"` is today's pre-P-registration-gating behavior
(anyone can `POST /api/v1/auth/register`); `"disabled"` rejects every
registration attempt with `AppError::Forbidden` before any DB work;
`"invite"` additionally requires a valid, unconsumed
`base_invitation_token` bearer matching the submitted email (Phase 2).
Same plain-`String` string-enum convention as `mfa_policy`/
`database.ssl_mode` — not a Rust enum.

require_verified_email.description:
P-account-lifecycle — when true, `attome_auth::accounts::login` rejects
(403) a local password account whose `email_verified` is still false.
Default false so air-gapped/no-SMTP deployments are unaffected; only
turn this on once `email.enabled` is also true, or every local account
locks itself out with no way to receive a verification link.

secure_cookies.description:
Gates the `Secure` flag on both auth cookies (Plan 1.6a). Default true —
only `config.debug.json` sets this false, so plain-http local dev keeps
working. `SameSite=Strict`/`HttpOnly` apply unconditionally either way.

access_key.description:
The storage account's shared access key. Presigned links are signed
with it, so it must be a key rather than a token.

container.description: The blob container that holds the files.

endpoint.description:
A custom endpoint (an Azurite emulator, a sovereign cloud). Empty (the
default) is the public Azure endpoint for the account.

dir.description:
Where archives go. Unset: a `backups` folder next to the
configuration file.

enabled.description: Run the daily backup. On by default.

files.description:
Copy the object store's files (attachments, brand assets) beside
each database backup. On by default.

hour.description: The hour of the day (UTC, 0–23) the backup runs.

keep.description: How many archives to keep, newest first. At least 1.

pg_dump.description: The `pg_dump` program. Unset: `pg_dump` on the PATH.

CacheBackend.description:
Where the platform keeps its shared, short-lived state: rate-limit
windows, replay nonces, revocation markers, caches and doorbells.
`docs/solo-memory-backend.md` is the design.

oneOf.description:
Redis or Dragonfly (Standard and Cluster, and Solo if one is
configured). The default.

Process memory. For Solo: one server process, no Redis to install. A
restart clears it, as a Redis restart without persistence would; every
value in it is short-lived or reconstructable. It is not a cross-node
source of truth, so a multi-node deployment must not use it.

sentinel.description:
P-redis-sentinel-config — see `CacheSection::sentinel`'s doc comment;
same meaning, scoped to this role's own endpoint.

tls_enabled.description:
P-datastore-tls — see `CacheSection::tls_enabled`. A role override
can point at a differently-secured endpoint than the base block.

CacheRoles.description:
P1.15 — role-specific Redis endpoint overrides, generalizing `CacheSection`
from one host/port to "one base block, optionally overridden per role."
Widen this struct (never replace the base block) when a new role needs its
own override.

coordination.description:
S2S nonce replay guard, S2S + general HTTP sliding-window rate limits,
and the idempotency `SET NX` gate — the "coordination-critical" keys
callable out in P1.15. A deployment can point these at a dedicated
Redis instance, isolated from general cache traffic (metadata pub/sub,
authz L2 cache), once its load demands it. Omit to keep everything on
the base `cache` block (today's default, unaffected).

backend.description:
`redis` (the default) or `memory`. With `memory`, `host`, `port`,
`password` and `db` are not used and may be left at any value.

connection_pool_size.description:
Pool size — plausibly scales with hardware/load. Has a default so a
deployment that hasn't tuned it can omit the key entirely.

encryption_key.description:
Z3-T3: the key ring a cache declared `EncryptedInRedis` seals its
values with before they reach Redis (AES-256-GCM, tagged with the key
id so a rotation keeps old entries readable). Required when such a
cache runs over Redis; such a cache refuses to start without it.

metadata_poll_interval_secs.description:
Y8-T2: how often a node checks the metadata change log for a change
whose doorbell it missed (a crash between commit and publish, a Redis
blip). The check is one indexed `MAX(id)`; 5 seconds bounds how stale
a node can be after a lost doorbell. At least 1.

metadata_registry_enabled.description:
Rollback switch for Plan 1.2 (kept for one release, not deleted): when
`false`, `resolve_entity` falls back to the pre-1.2 direct Postgres
query path instead of the arc-swap metadata registry.

roles.description:
P1.15 — optional per-role endpoint overrides. `None` (the default)
means every role shares this base block, identical to pre-P1.15
behavior. See `CacheRole`/`AppConfig::redis_url_for_role`.

sentinel.description:
P-redis-sentinel-config — closes the self-host HA tier's documented
app-wiring gap (scale-out-ops skill / P-ha-failover-hardening):
`create_redis_pool` previously only spoke a fixed `host:port`, so a
Sentinel-fronted deployment needed an operator-managed proxy/VIP in
front of Sentinel's resolved master. `None` (the default) is
byte-for-byte today's centralized-connection behavior. Set this to
connect via fred's `redis-sentinel://` scheme instead, whose documented
contract is to re-resolve the current master through the sentinel quorum
on every (re)connect — `host`/`port` above then name the first known
sentinel node, not the Redis server itself.

**Unproven here (BCA-55).** Re-resolving *a* master is fred's behaviour,
not something this repo has ever exercised: no test or drill has failed
a Sentinel quorum over and confirmed the pool follows, which is why
D-153's "not verified" item 3 still stands and scale-out-ops does not
yet present Sentinel as a supported recipe. Treat a Sentinel deployment
as unvalidated until BCA-55 records a failover result; the plain-restart
half (reconnect without a process restart) is proven — BCA-01/BCA-01b.

timeout.description:
Connect/command timeout in milliseconds — plausibly varies with
network latency.

tls_ca_path.description:
P-datastore-tls — path to a CA certificate file (PEM) to pin, instead
of trusting the system/default root store. Only meaningful when
`tls_enabled` is true.

tls_enabled.description:
P-datastore-tls — connect via `rediss://` (fred's TLS-enabled scheme)
instead of `redis://`. Default false — byte-for-byte identical to
pre-TLS behavior when unset.

CacheSentinelConfig.description:
Sentinel-mode connection details for a `CacheSection`/`CacheRoleOverride`
block (P-redis-sentinel-config). The enclosing block's `host`/`port`
name the first known sentinel node; `nodes` lists any additional sentinel
nodes for quorum. The enclosing block's `password` still authenticates to
the resolved master/replica (unchanged meaning) — `sentinel_username`/
`sentinel_password` here are separate credentials for the sentinel nodes
themselves, only honored under fred's `sentinel-auth` feature (enabled
workspace-wide, see root `Cargo.toml`). Leave them unset when the
sentinel nodes require no auth of their own, which most deployments do
(Sentinel exposes no customer data — see `deploy/ha/sentinel.conf.example`).

service_name.description:
Fred's `sentinelServiceName` — the name Sentinel knows the monitored
master by (often `mymaster`). Required whenever `sentinel` is set.

enforcement_enabled.description:
Whether a confirmed-unavailable capability actually rejects requests
on the routes that declare it, or is only reported.

Defaults **on**, deliberately unlike most flags in this config tree:
the finding D-344 answers is that the platform currently accepts work
it cannot complete, and shipping the fix dark would not fix it. The
blast radius is bounded by construction — only the handful of routes
that name `attome_server::capability::Available<C>`, only after
[`Self::failure_threshold`] *consecutive* failed probes, cleared by a
single success. Setting this to `false` (with `probe_enabled = true`)
is the intended rollout mode for an operator who wants to watch
`/health/dependencies`'s `capabilities` block for a while first, and
is also the kill switch if a probe ever proves flaky against a
particular backend.

failure_threshold.description:
Consecutive failed probes before a capability flips to
`unavailable`. 2 (i.e. up to ~60s at the default interval) rather than
1: a single dropped connection to S3 or a relay is normal background
noise and must not start rejecting uploads. A single success clears
the counter immediately — slow to trip, fast to recover.

probe_enabled.description:
Whether `xrm_server::spawn_capability_refresh` should run at all.
`false` leaves every capability at `unknown` forever, which the gate
treats as "pass" — byte-identical to the behavior before D-344, same
"nothing happens unless the poll task is spawned" posture as
`audit.ingest_backlog_threshold`'s breaker.

probe_interval_secs.description:
Seconds between probe rounds. 30s, not the 15s a readiness probe
would use: this drives a route gate, not traffic routing, and the SMTP
probe opens a real TCP+TLS connection to the relay each round — a
tighter loop is a connection-rate cost paid against every deployment's
mail provider for no decision-making benefit.

worker_stale_after_secs.description:
How stale (`apalis.workers.last_seen`, via
`attome_jobs::worker_last_seen_age_seconds`) a queue's worker heartbeat
may be before that queue counts as a failed probe. 90s matches the
`ApalisWorkerStale` alert rule's own expression
(`observability/alerts.yml`) — 3 missed 30s `keep_alive` beats — so
the gate and the alert can never disagree about what "the worker is
down" means.

pow_difficulty.description: Q20-T3: leading zero bits a proof-of-work answer needs, 1 to 24.

oneOf.description:
Q20-T3: a self-hosted proof-of-work challenge
(`attome_auth::pow`); no outside service and no secret to configure.

adapter.description:
The adapter that calls it. Only `openai_compatible` exists today
(Z9-T1); native adapters arrive with Z9-T2.

allowed_labels.description:
The labels of content it may be sent. Defaults to `public` and
`internal`: a model receives personal, financial or health data only
when an operator says so.

cost_per_1k_tokens.description:
What 1,000 tokens cost, in the deployment's currency. 0 for a
self-hosted model with no per-token price.

id.description: The model id requested from the provider, recorded on every output.

max_concurrent.description:
Z9-T6: how many calls a self-hosted model serves at once (default 4);
more wait their turn. Ignored for a hosted model.

max_context.description: The largest context it accepts, in tokens.

self_hosted.description:
Whether it runs inside the deployment. Only self-hosted models receive
`secret` content, or any content when
`inference.allow_external_provider` is off.

retention_days.description:
Floor for `PlatformJob::PruneChangeFeed`: how long a fully-processed
`xrm_core_entity_change_event` row is kept before it becomes eligible
for deletion. This is a floor, not a target — `xrm_foundation::
change_feed::prune` additionally never deletes a row the slowest
registered consumer cursor has not passed, however old it is, so
raising this only ever makes pruning MORE conservative, never less.

ChangesetLayer.description:
The four owner layers (D-785 rule 2), lowest first. The wire and column
form is [`Self::as_str`].

auto_layer.description:
The layer of automatic changesets. Phase 1 accepts only `project`;
Phase 3 adds `customer` together with its authoring rules.

mode.description:
`required`: a metadata admin write with no open changeset is refused
(409 `changeset_required`). `auto`: each request's writes become one
closed automatic changeset. Unset means `auto` on every profile, so a
config written before changesets existed (the production templates,
every hand-written test config) keeps working unchanged; a
development deployment opts into `required` explicitly, as
`config.example.json` does. Read it through [`Self::effective_mode`],
never this field directly.

allowed_origins.description:
Explicit allow-list of origins (scheme + host + port), e.g.
"https://app.example.com". Never a wildcard alongside credentials.
When empty, `AppConfig::allowed_origins` derives a dev-only default
from `app.frontend_host`/`app.frontend_port` (always `http://` — set
this explicitly for any deployment behind TLS).

DataLabel.description:
Z9-T3 — a data sensitivity label (A1), lowest to highest. A request
carries the highest label of the content it sends; a model receives it
only when the label is in its `allowed_labels`.

oneOf.description: Never leaves the deployment: only a self-hosted model receives it.

DatabasePoolSize.description: One pool's size override; `max_connections` is validated to `1..=1000`.

DatabasePools.description:
attome-db hardening Phase 2.3 — `database.pools`: optional per-pool sizes.
A pool with no entry is sized from `DatabaseSection::connection_number`.

long.description:
AB6-T6: the long pool reports and exports read through (the
`attome_readonly` role on the primary), so they never take a
connection an interactive request needs.

connection_number.description:
Pool size — plausibly scales with hardware/load. Has a default so a
deployment that hasn't tuned it can omit the key entirely.

direct_url.description:
P1.12 — a raw `postgres://` URL used ONLY for schema bootstrap +
migrations (`attome_db::create_direct_pool`), bypassing whatever
`host`/`port` above point at. Set this when `host`/`port` point at a
transaction-mode pgbouncer, since `sqlx::migrate!`'s internal
session-level advisory lock is unsafe under transaction pooling.
`None` (the default — no pgbouncer in front of this deployment) falls
back to `database_url()`, i.e. identical to today's behavior. Stays
on `user`/`password` even when `migrator` above is configured — see
`AppConfig::direct_database_url`'s doc comment (P-db-privilege-
separation) for why.

disable_statement_cache.description:
P1.12 — disables sqlx's client-side prepared-statement cache. Found
necessary while actually load-testing the pgbouncer recipe (P1.8d
step 5, 2026-07-21, D-106): a transaction-mode pgbouncer without
protocol-level prepared-statement support (added in pgbouncer 1.21)
can hand a client's logical connection a different real backend
between transactions, so a statement sqlx cached as prepared on one
backend does not exist on the next — surfacing as `prepared
statement "sqlx_s_N" already exists` or "does not exist" under real
concurrent load. D-171: `pgbouncer/Dockerfile` (this platform's
reference recipe) moved off the Debian bookworm apt package (1.18)
onto a maintained >=1.21 image, so this flag is no longer needed for
that recipe by default — it remains a general escape hatch for any
deployment fronted by a pre-1.21 pooler. Set this `true` whenever
`database.host`/`port` point at such a pooler; `false` (the default —
no behavior change for a direct-to-Postgres deployment) keeps the
cache on.

failover_pin_secs.description:
AB2-T4: after the database's leader changes (a failover), every read goes
to the primary for this many seconds, so a person never reads an older
replica than the write they just made while replicas catch up to the new
leader. 0 turns it off; at most 300.

max_server_connections.description:
Z2-T2: PostgreSQL's (or pgbouncer's) `max_connections`, when known.
`None` assumes 100 once sizing applies.

migrate_on_boot.description:
P-db-privilege-separation follow-up (§1's "move migrations to a
one-shot deployment job"). `true` (the default — today's behavior,
unchanged) keeps `main.rs`'s inline `ensure_schema`, `run_migrations`,
and role-password-seed sequence on every server boot, same as before
this flag existed. Set `false` once a deployment's release process
runs the dedicated `migrate` binary (`crates/server/src/bin/migrate.rs`,
same `direct_database_url()` bootstrap identity, same migration set)
as its own one-shot step ahead of starting/rolling any `server`
process — the point being that the long-lived web process no longer
needs to hold `CREATE ROLE`/DDL-capable bootstrap credentials at all
once its deploy pipeline guarantees migrations already ran. `server`
does not verify the schema is current when this is `false`; an
operator who flips it without wiring the `migrate` step first will see
ordinary runtime queries fail against a stale schema, not a boot error.

migrator.description:
P-db-privilege-separation / D-117 — DDL-capable identity for runtime
entity/attribute provisioning (`xrm-entity::provision`) and boot-time
entity seeding, reusing this section's host/port/dbname/schema, only
the credentials differ (same shape as `readonly`). Deliberately NOT
used for schema bootstrap/`sqlx::migrate!` — see
`AppConfig::direct_database_url`'s doc comment for why that stays on
`user`/`password` forever. `None` (the default) falls back to
`user`/`password` above — today's behavior, unchanged. Set this once
`migrations/0042_migrator_runtime_roles.sql`'s `attome_migrator` role
exists and has had a login password applied
(`server::db_role_seed::seed_migrator`).

Fail-closed follow-up (supersedes D-117's original "additive, not
fail-closed" framing — see DECISIONS.md): `main.rs` now refuses to
boot with this unset outside `APP_ENV=debug`, same posture as
`readonly` above (D-038). This field stays genuinely optional for
local dev; the fallback above just isn't reachable in production
without an explicit `APP_ENV=debug` opt-out anymore.

node_count.description:
Z2-T2: how many processes share this database. With more than one,
or with `max_server_connections` set, a pool with no
`database.pools` entry is sized from PostgreSQL's connection budget
split across the nodes instead of from `connection_number`.

password.description:
P-bootstrap-credential-scoping (D-204) — the schema-bootstrap/
`CREATE ROLE`-capable identity (`database_url()`/`direct_database_url()`),
needed ONLY by the one-shot `migrate` binary and, when
`migrate_on_boot = true`, by the inline bootstrap sequence in
`boot::init`. `server`/`worker` never legitimately reach either code
path once `migrate_on_boot = false` and `migrator`/`runtime` below are
configured (D-148) — so a deployment that renders those two
processes' `config.json` without this field (and without `DB_PASSWORD`
in their `.env`) keeps the bootstrap credential out of their container
environment and out of the `AppState` they hold in memory for the
life of the process, instead of it merely going unused. `None` is
valid whenever nothing in this process can reach `database_url()`;
`validate()` enforces `Some` when `migrate_on_boot = true`, and
`bin/migrate.rs` independently requires `Some` unconditionally (that
binary is not gated by `migrate_on_boot` — see its own module doc).

pools.description:
attome-db hardening Phase 2.3 — optional per-pool sizes. A pool with no
entry here is sized from `connection_number`, so omitting the whole
block keeps today's behavior. Each value must be `1..=1000`
(`AppConfig::validate`). The direct pool (schema bootstrap and
migrations) keeps its fixed size of 2 and has no entry.

readonly.description:
SELECT-only role for `/api/v1/query/execute` (P1.1e) — reuses this
section's host/port/dbname/schema, only the credentials differ.

replica_max_lag_secs.description:
P-ha-failover-hardening item (e), D-125 — consumed by
`AppState::route_if_lag_ok` (P-read-your-writes-lsn) as an
unconditional circuit breaker: whenever
`replica_watermark::ReplicaWatermark.lag_seconds` (the always-on
poller's cached value, `AppState.replica_watermark`) exceeds this
threshold, every routed read falls back to the primary regardless of
any specific user's pin. Also widens `pin_write_with_lsn`'s effective
TTL to `max(sticky_primary_ttl_secs, replica_max_lag_secs)` so the
pin never expires before this policy's own declared lag tolerance
(`P-read-your-writes-lsn.md` §4(6)). `None` (the default) means "no
max-lag policy configured" — today's behavior, unchanged: no circuit
breaker, and the TTL formula reduces to `sticky_primary_ttl_secs`
alone.

runtime.description:
P-db-privilege-separation / D-117 — DML-only identity for ordinary
request-time record CRUD (`attome_db::create_pool`, the pool
`AppState.db`/entity_crud.rs uses). Same shape as `readonly`/
`migrator`. `None` (the default) falls back to `user`/`password` —
today's behavior, unchanged. This is a separate optional field, not a
repurposing of `user`/`password` themselves, specifically so
`user`/`password` can stay the schema-bootstrap identity
(`direct_database_url()`, needs DDL/`CREATE ROLE` for migrations like
0042 itself) while this identity is locked down to DML — the two
requirements are incompatible on one shared credential. Set this once
migration 0042's `attome_runtime` role exists and has had a login
password applied (`server::db_role_seed::seed_runtime`).

Fail-closed follow-up (supersedes D-117's original "additive, not
fail-closed" framing — see DECISIONS.md): `main.rs` now refuses to
boot with this unset outside `APP_ENV=debug`, same posture as
`readonly` above (D-038). This field stays genuinely optional for
local dev; the fallback above just isn't reachable in production
without an explicit `APP_ENV=debug` opt-out anymore.

ssl_mode.description:
P-datastore-tls — one of Postgres's six `sslmode` values: "disable",
"allow", "prefer" (the default — matches sqlx's own default, so
unset is byte-for-byte identical to pre-TLS behavior), "require",
"verify-ca", "verify-full". Validated against this fixed set at boot
(`AppConfig::validate`, D-038) — `attome-db` parses the validated
string into `sqlx::postgres::PgSslMode`, kept out of this crate to
avoid a `sqlx` dependency here (attome-config stays DB-agnostic).

ssl_root_cert.description:
P-datastore-tls — path to a CA certificate file (PEM) used by
"verify-ca"/"verify-full" modes. Deployment-provided (D-002: one
customer, one set of certs) — no CA machinery lives in this platform.

statement_classes.description:
Z2-T5: per statement class, the statement, lock and
idle-in-transaction timeouts that replace the class defaults. A class
left out keeps its defaults.

sticky_primary_ttl_secs.description:
P1.12 — TTL (seconds) of the Redis "just wrote" pin
(`attome-db:rw-pin:{user_id}`) that `AppState::read_pool` checks before
routing a read to `readonly` instead of the primary. Widen this if a
deployment's replica routinely lags past the default window.

timeout.description:
Pool **acquire** timeout in seconds, fractional allowed (`0.5` is
500ms): how long a caller waits for a pooled connection, which
includes opening a new one. Also bounds the connect of attome-db's
unpooled direct/migrator connections. `AppConfig::validate` requires a
finite value in `(0, 120]`.

DeploymentSection.description:
Declares the region this deployment's data is contractually/
regulatorily supposed to stay in (e.g. `"bh-1"`, `"eu-west-1"`) — a
residency *claim*, not itself an enforcement mechanism. Paired with
`AppConfig::validate`'s boot-time check, which asserts this matches
`storage.s3_region`: the platform's per-customer dedicated data-plane
model (D-001/D-002) already places a customer's whole stack in-region, so
this doesn't enforce residency itself — it only catches the declared
region silently drifting out of sync with where the object store/backup
endpoint actually is. Also consumed by
`xrm_foundation::assert_transfer_allowed` (via `state.base.config`) as
the "deployment_region" side of the cross-border transfer-restriction
gate on every export path.

`None` (the default) means no residency claim is configured — both the
boot-time validator and the transfer gate are then a no-op, "ships dark"
like every other opt-in section added this session
(`retention`/`idempotency`/`approval`).

`bundle_ref`/`bundle_signing_public_key` (P-environment-promotion §5 step
23 — the F273 `APP_VERTICAL` loader generalized) declare a signed
`attome-bundle/v1` artifact this deployment pulls and applies: `bundle_ref`
is a file path or `https://` URL to `{ "bundle": <canonical bundle JSON>,
"signature": "<base64 Ed25519 over the canonical bundle bytes>" }`, and
`bundle_signing_public_key` is the base64 Ed25519 public key that artifact
must verify against (same key-format/verify primitives
`xrm-license::verifier` uses, so an artifact `bundle-tool` signs verifies
with the identical machinery a license does). Both `None` (the default) is
"not configured" — `bundle::pull::fetch_and_verify` is then a no-op and
nothing changes about boot. Configuring one without the other is a boot
error (`AppConfig::validate`): a bundle without a key could never be
verified, and a key with nothing to verify configures nothing.

outbound_proxy.description:
Q21-T1: an HTTP(S) proxy for calls to public addresses (vendor APIs,
webhooks), for a network that reaches the internet only through one,
such as `http://proxy.corp:3128` (credentials may be in the URL).
Hosts the operator lists as private for a call (a model server, an
identity provider) are reached directly. `HTTP_PROXY` and the other
environment variables are never used. Absent means no proxy.

portal_hosts.description:
D-585: the hosts web portals (`/{keyword}/...`) answer on, disjoint
from `staff_hosts`. Empty means portals answer on any host outside
the production profile, and on **no** host in it.

read_only_at_database_bytes.description:
AB5-T6: when the database reaches this many bytes the deployment
turns read-only, before the disk fills. Absent means no ceiling.

sovereign.description:
U1-T5, the sovereign preset: when true, boot refuses any configured
destination outside this deployment (object store, SMTP relay, model
servers, identity providers, trace collector, render service) and any
outside AI provider, so the deployment makes no outbound connection
its operator did not name. See `AppConfig::sovereign_violations`.

sovereign_allowed_hosts.description:
Host names a sovereign deployment may still reach although they are
not on its own network: the organisation's own mail relay or identity
provider, for example. Exact, lowercase host names.

staff_hosts.description:
D-585: the hosts the staff app and `/api/v1` answer on. Empty means
"any host" (today's behaviour), and is refused once `portal_hosts` is
set: a portal host must never also serve the staff API.

max_html_bytes.description:
Cap on the merged HTML document sent to the sidecar — bounds both the
request body and the amount of markup the SSRF-shaped external-URL
scan (`xrm_docgen::ssrf`) has to walk.

max_response_bytes.description: Cap on the rendered PDF response read back from the sidecar.

sendgrid_public_key.description:
SendGrid's signed event webhook verification key (the base64
SubjectPublicKeyInfo SendGrid shows); unset refuses SendGrid events.

ses_topic_arns.description:
The SNS topics (ARNs) whose SES notifications are accepted; empty
refuses SES events.

EmailProviders.description:
Z8-T1: `email.providers`. `by_sender` maps a From address (any case) to
a provider name; every other address takes `default`, SMTP when unset.
A provider named here needs its own block below.

EmailRateLimits.description:
Z8-T3: `email.rate_limits`. Each stream's own limits; a stream with
none set sends as fast as the provider takes it.

enabled.description:
P-account-lifecycle — this section existed but nothing consumed it
(dead config, audit finding E). `enabled` is the explicit opt-in: when
false, `attome-email` is never constructed and reset/verification
requests return 503 `feature_unavailable` instead of silently trying
(and failing) to reach an SMTP host that was never meant to be live —
same "ships dark behind a flag" pattern as `audit.chainer_enabled`.

feedback.description:
Z8-T5: where providers report bounces, complaints and unsubscribes
(`POST /api/v1/email/webhooks/{provider}`). Nothing is accepted from a
provider not configured here.

providers.description:
Z8-T1: which provider sends a message: SMTP (the fields above, the
default), Amazon SES or SendGrid, chosen per sender identity.

rate_limits.description:
Z8-T3: messages per minute, per stream. Transactional mail (sign-in
codes, resets, notifications) and bulk mail (surveys, campaigns) each
have their own limits, so a campaign never holds up a sign-in code.
Paced per worker node: a send over a limit waits for the minute to
turn (up to a minute), then retries later.

smtp_use_tls.description:
**Deprecated** (BEM-5): `true` = implicit TLS, `false` = plaintext.
Superseded by [`Self::tls_mode`], which wins when both are set; kept
deserializable for one release so an existing `config.json` keeps
booting, and warned about by `validate()` so operators migrate.
`Option` rather than `bool` so "absent" is distinguishable from an
explicit `false` — the old key was mandatory, so an absent one means
the file was written after the `tls_mode` rename.

test_mode_catch_all.description:
Z8-T6: test mode. When set, every email goes to this one address
instead of its recipients (named in an `X-Attome-Original-To`
header), so a development or copied deployment never mails a real
person.

tls_mode.description:
The SMTP transport security mode (BEM-5, attome-email plan §4.3):
`"implicit"` (SMTPS, the default), `"starttls"` (upgrade required —
lettre aborts if the relay does not offer it), or `"none"` (plaintext,
refused outside `APP_ENV=debug`). Validated by `validate()`.

A `String`, not an enum: the value crosses the `attome-config` boundary
into `attome-email`'s transport builder, and this section's module is
`pub(crate)` — a new public enum would need a re-export in
`config/mod.rs` and `lib.rs`, which BEM-5 does not own.

EmailStreamRates.description: Z8-T3: one stream's limits, in messages per minute.

domains.description:
By recipient domain, any case: `{"gmail.com": 120}`. A domain not
named has no limit.

providers.description:
By provider name (`"smtp"`, `"ses"`, `"sendgrid"`):
`{"ses": 600}`. A provider not named has no limit.

dispatch_batch_size.description:
Bound on how many outbox events one dispatcher tick reads per active
subscription (M62 plan §3 "Bounded batch").

webhook_signing_key.description:
P-key-rotation-and-jwt (a) trust domain for signing outbound webhook
deliveries, deliberately **separate** from `s2s.key_encryption_key`
(D-069's "machine-auth secrets and human/other secrets are separate
trust domains; a compromise or rotation of one key must never
implicate the other" — S2S authenticates *inbound* machine calls,
this key signs *outbound* payloads sent to a subscriber-controlled
URL, so the two must be independently rotatable).

changesets_dir.description:
Where closed `attome-changeset/v1` files are read from (the developer
runs the source tree, design §6.4).

credential_encryption_key.description:
Encrypts each customer's rollout S2S secret at rest. Required (and
checked) only when the console is requested with
`ATTOME_FLEET_CONSOLE=1`; well formed whenever it is set.

notify_user_refs.description:
Who the F3 notifications go to. Empty: every active `system.admin`
holder of the developer's database.

poll_interval_secs.description: How often the gated `FleetPoll` scheduler syncs every customer.

request_timeout_secs.description: Bound on one outbound call to a customer server.

bucket.description: The bucket that holds the files.

service_account_key.description:
The service account key, as the JSON document Google issues. Presigned
links are signed with its private key.

GoogleAiSection.description:
Only `api_key` is a real per-deployment credential today — no engine
crate calls the Gemini API yet, so
`base_url`/`default_model`/`timeout_seconds` were dropped (D-099-era
scaffolding for a feature that was never wired up); reintroduce them
alongside whatever crate actually builds the client once one exists.

bulk_retention_hours.description:
S9-T2: how long a bulk job's durable record is kept (a bulk job may
be retried days later). Seven days by default.

durable_retention_hours.description:
How long a completed `base_idempotency_record` row is kept before
`PlatformJob::PruneIdempotencyRecords` soft-deletes it. Same default
window as the Redis tier's TTL (`idempotency.rs::TTL_SECS`).

mandatory_operations.description:
Operation-name strings (`"{METHOD} {route-template}"`, e.g.
`"POST /api/v1/{entity}/bulk"` — the same string
`attome_server::middleware::idempotency::operation_name` derives via
axum's `MatchedPath`) that must go through the durable Postgres tier
(`base_idempotency_record`, migration `0066`) instead of the default
Redis-only gate, and must require `X-Idempotency-Key` outright (a
missing header on a listed route is `422 Validation`, not a silent
skip). Empty by default — a deployment opts in explicitly.

Validated at boot, not here: `AppConfig::validate()` has no
visibility into the router (route templates are assembled in
`crates/server`/`xrm-server`, several layers above `attome-config`), so
`server::boot::init`'s `validate_operation_registries` (the
composition root, which depends on both this crate and `xrm-server`)
checks every entry here against `xrm_server::bulk::
MANDATORY_TIER_OPERATIONS` and fails the boot closed on an
unrecognized one, instead of silently never matching. D-327: the same
function also fails boot closed when `app.deployment_profile =
"production"` and this list is empty or missing any
`MANDATORY_TIER_OPERATIONS` entry — `config.production.example.json`
ships with the full list already filled in for exactly this reason.

replay_max_bytes.description:
Largest successful response body the Redis idempotency gate stores
for replay. A larger response still reaches the client in full, but a
same-key retry gets `idempotency_replay_unavailable` instead of a
replay. Bounds how much a single cached response can put on the
coordination Redis. Must be at least 1.

response_encryption_key.description:
S9-T3: the key ring that seals a durable record's stored response
(AES-256-GCM, tagged with the key id, bound to the record's id). Unset
stores responses as they are; set it on any deployment whose
responses carry personal data. Keep a retired key in the ring until
the records it sealed are past `bulk_retention_hours`.

InferenceEndpoint.description:
One model endpoint. Both the generation server and the embedding server
speak the same OpenAI-compatible HTTP surface (D-360 ruling 3), so one
shape describes either.

base_url.description:
Base URL of the serving process, e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1`.
Empty means "not configured", which the client reports as unavailable
rather than attempting a request to an empty host.

model.description:
The model id to request. Recorded on every suggestion as provenance
(`model_id`), so an auditor can answer "which model wrote this" — see
TODO-054.

request_timeout_secs.description:
Per-request timeout. Generation is slow by nature and a bare default
would either cut off a legitimate long answer or hang a request thread
for minutes; naming it per endpoint lets the embedding endpoint keep a
tight bound while generation gets a loose one.

allow_external_provider.description:
Whether [`Self::generation`]/[`Self::embedding`] may point outside the
data plane.

**Default false, and load-bearing.** With local inference a prompt
never leaves the customer's plane and no classification event is
raised. Pointing the same client at a third-party API means every
prompt — case notes, customer names, whatever the record holds — is
customer data leaving the plane, classified under the existing
`0087`/`0088` scheme and audited at the moment it is enabled. An
air-gapped deployment must fail at boot if this is true, not at first
use: "we discovered we were sending case notes to a third party" is
not an acceptable way to find out.

caller_token_budget_per_min.description:
BIN-D7 — deprecated: accepted and ignored, nothing enforces it (the
per-caller budget lives in `xrm-ai`'s budget guard). Kept for one
release so an existing config still loads; boot warns when it is set
(`AppConfig::deprecated_keys`), then the field goes.

catalogue.description:
Z9-T3 — the model catalogue the router picks from: each model's
capabilities, context size, cost and the data labels it may be sent.
Empty by default: nothing is routed by catalogue, and every task runs
on `generation` (or its `task_models` entry) as before.

embedding.description:
Embeddings. Separate serving process from generation by design — one
vLLM instance serves one task, so the VRAM split is a deployment
sizing decision rather than a runtime surprise (D-360 ruling 3).

embedding_document_prefix.description:
Prefix prepended to every **document** text before it is embedded.
See [`Self::embedding_query_prefix`].

embedding_query_prefix.description:
Prefix prepended to every **query** text before it is embedded,
overriding the model-family heuristic (BIN-D6/BIN-G5).

Asymmetric embedding models (E5, Qwen3) need one prefix for a query and
another for a document, and getting it wrong degrades recall silently
rather than erroring. The heuristic here recognises the families it
knows; this key makes the answer explicit for any model it does not,
and an explicit empty string means "no prefix" — which is how a
deployment turns the heuristic off. Lives on the section rather than on
[`InferenceEndpoint`] because only embedding has prefixes, and because
an endpoint is also built in code where an exhaustive literal exists.

knowledge_article_data_source.description:
The Data Source (UUID, as text) new drafts are filed under.

Required only when the target article entity is the Knowledge Base item,
whose `data_source_ref` lookup is required. A draft is filed by
configuration rather than by the model, because "which container does
this belong in" is a governance decision an operator makes once, not a
model makes per draft. Left unset, a draft against the KB item fails
with a validation error naming this key rather than writing an orphan.

knowledge_article_entity.description:
The entity `article.draft` writes into (TODO-060).

Configuration rather than a constant because entities are
**provisioned at runtime through the admin API** (I-8), so a deployment
is free to name its own article entity.

**Defaults to `xrm_knowledge_data_item`** — the entity D-489 makes the
canonical Knowledge Base article, whose chunks the `xrm-search` drain
projects. Before D-489 the default was `None`, so `article.draft`
refused to run on a stock deployment; now the case→draft loop works
out of the box. Setting it to `null` still disables the action.

A deployment *can* override the name, but only where `article.draft`
writes changes: the chunking drain and gap-queue retrieval are
hardcoded to the canonical entity's own columns, not to this value, so
an override to anything other than `xrm_knowledge_data_item` gets
drafts written but never chunked or retrievable — `boot.rs`'s
`warn_if_knowledge_article_entity_diverges` logs exactly this at
startup rather than failing silently.

max_output_tokens.description:
Maximum tokens one request may generate. Bounds a runaway loop and
makes latency predictable enough to set a timeout against.

ocr.description:
Reading text from images (N21-T1): a vision-language model behind an
OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint. Documents are customer data, so it
must be inside the deployment. Empty `base_url` means OCR is off.

provider_credential_key.description:
Encrypts `xrm_ai_provider_credential.secret_encrypted` at rest — the
API key an operator gives an `xrm_ai_provider` record so the platform
can list that provider's models.

Its own [`KeyRing`] and its own trust domain (D-069), deliberately
separate from `integration.credential_encryption_key`: both hold "a
third party's secret", but connector credentials and AI provider keys
are held by different operators and rotated on different schedules, so
a compromise or rotation of one must not implicate the other. Never
used to sign or verify anything.

Empty by default: a deployment that never sets a provider API key
never needs this configured, and the credential route refuses with an
operator-actionable error rather than encrypting under an absent key.

rerank.description:
Reranking knowledge passages (N15-T1): a cross-encoder behind TEI's
`/rerank`. Inside the deployment only. Empty `base_url`: no reranking,
passages keep their fused order.

speech.description:
Speech to text (N22-T1): an OpenAI-compatible transcription server.
Recordings are customer data, so it must be inside the deployment.
Empty `base_url` means transcription is off.

spend.description:
N24-T1 — money budgets for generation. Empty by default: no prices,
no money budgets, only the token budgets apply.

task_models.description:
N25-T1 — which approved catalogue model (`ai_model` id) a task runs
on, by action id (or `agent.turn` for chat and agent turns). A task
not listed runs on `generation`.

request_timeout_secs.description:
Bound on how long the REST adapter's outbound HTTP client waits for a
pull/push/health call to an external system, mirroring
`WebcrawlSection::request_timeout_secs`'s per-feature timeout
convention rather than a shared global constant.

batch_worker_concurrency.description:
P-job-queue-hardening (D-165) — max in-flight jobs the *batch* queue's
worker processes concurrently. The batch set is exactly the variants
`PlatformJob::is_batch` returns `true` for — the open-ended,
record-count-proportional kinds (`BulkEntityOperation`,
`ApplyStagedImport`, `RewrapSecrets`, `ApplySchemaChangePlan`,
`ApplyMetadataBundle`, `CrawlWebsite`, `CascadeDeactivateDependents`,
`DataExport`, `DataProfile`, `DataBulkTransform`,
`RollbackMigrationRun`, `ReportRun`, `LegalMatterCollect`,
`LegalMatterRelease`). That
method is the authority; this list is a reading aid, not a second copy
to keep in sync.
Lower default than the fast queue's: these are individually heavier
per unit of concurrency.

dead_letter_retention_days.description:
BJB-15 (attome-jobs plan) — how long a dead-lettered (`Killed`)
`apalis.jobs` row is kept before `PlatformJob::PruneApalisJobHistory`
deletes it. The same sweep, a longer window: a `Done` row is history,
but an untriaged dead letter is the operator's only record that a job
kept failing, so it outlives the history window and its deletion is
logged with a count. Every dead letter the sweep deletes is a row an
operator never replayed, discarded or investigated (BJB-F9).

Plain serde default; no production-profile rule belongs in
`loader.rs` for it — the value is neither a secret nor a
safety-critical switch, so it is not validated there.

history_retention_days.description:
P-job-queue-hardening (D-165) — how long a terminal (`Done`/`Killed`)
`apalis.jobs` row is kept before `PlatformJob::PruneApalisJobHistory`
deletes it. Keeps the dead-letter admin list and the table itself
bounded; apalis never vacuums a finished job on its own.

run_worker_inline.description:
P-worker-process-split — `true` (default, today's behavior unchanged)
runs the apalis job `Monitor` inline inside the `server` process, same
as before this flag existed. A deployment that has split the worker
out into its own process/container (`crates/server/src/bin/worker.rs`,
scaled and deployed independently of the HTTP tier) sets this `false`
so `server` never builds/runs the `Monitor` or spawns the partition/
upload-session maintenance schedulers — those move to `worker`
entirely, avoiding double-enqueue from two schedulers ticking at once.
Same "off by default until an operator opts in" posture as
`database.migrate_on_boot`.

worker_concurrency.description:
Max in-flight `PlatformJob`s the fast-queue worker processes
concurrently. Tuned against `database.connection_number` (§14.1) —
the remaining fast-queue work is low-volume and low-CPU, not a pool
hog. (The API-key/S2S "touch" writes that used to be the bulk of it
moved off apalis onto the Redis stream / coalescing-hash path in
D-164.)

workflow_payload_retention_days.description:
M3-T4 — how long a finished workflow step keeps its recorded input
and output before the daily prune clears them (the step's summary
stays).

KdfSection.description:
`auth.kdf` — see [`AuthSection::kdf`]. Every default is the value the
release-build benchmark in `document/base/auth/kdf-benchmark-2026-09-14.md`
chose; raise the Argon2 costs only with a new measurement.

acquire_timeout_ms.description: How long a request waits for a KDF permit before a 503 (100..=30000).

argon2_m_cost.description: Argon2id memory cost in KiB for new hashes. OWASP floor 19456.

argon2_t_cost.description: Argon2id passes for new hashes. OWASP floor 2.

hard_cap.description: Upper bound on concurrent KDF operations whatever the host (1..=64).

memory_budget_bytes.description:
Memory all concurrent KDF operations may use together; must fit at
least one operation.

password_min_length.description: Minimum password length in characters (floor 12, security contract I2).

path.description:
The folder that holds the files. Created at boot when it does not
exist. Required with the local backend.

public_base_url.description:
Address browsers reach the server at, put in front of the signed
links (`https://crm.example.com`). Empty (the default) hands out links
relative to the server, which a browser on the same origin follows.

url_signing_key.description:
Key that signs the short-lived upload and download links the server
hands out in place of presigned bucket URLs (at least 32 bytes). Every
process of the deployment needs the same value, so a link one process
mints is accepted by another.

MetadataSection.description:
`metadata` — additive, every field defaulted, so a config file without it
keeps today's behaviour: an unset mode is `auto` (see
[`ChangesetsSection::mode`]).

backfill_batch_max.description: Y12-T6: the largest batch a backfill grows to. Unset is 50,000.

quiet_hours.description:
Y12-T6: the local hours (`"01-05"`, end not included) when a
backfill may grow its batches. Unset is 01:00 to 05:00.

recovery_archive_key_encryption_key.description:
Solution 7 Phase 2 (D-788 rule 9): the key-encryption-key ring of the
30-day recovery archive (`xrm_core_recovery_archive`), its own trust
domain (D-069). Empty (the default) means "not configured": every
operation that would archive a value (a field delete with values, a
type change that nulls values) is refused with `archive_key_missing`
(fail closed). When set, every entry must be 64 hex chars (a boot
error otherwise). `KeyRing`'s `Debug` redacts the values.

release_report.description:
Solution 7 Phase 2 (design §10.5): the post-apply release-report
notification.

storage_tuning_enabled.description:
Y2-T9: the daily table-health job also sets each entity table's fill
factor from its measured updates (80 for a table whose updates miss
heap-only updates, 100 for an append-only one). Off by default.

MigratorDbCredentials.description:
P-db-privilege-separation / D-117 — same shape as `ReadonlyDbCredentials`,
for the DDL-capable `attome_migrator` role.

ModelCapability.description: Z9-T3 — what a catalogue model can do.

ModelPrice.description: One model's price per million tokens.

NotificationSection.description:
Notification recipient retention is deliberately opt-in. A zero value
disables pruning, matching the audit retention convention while avoiding
an unexpected destructive default for existing deployments.

email_from.description:
M51 Phase 1 — the "From" header notification-engine email should
appear to come from (e.g. `"Notifications <notifications@example.com>"`),
distinct from the account-lifecycle "From" in `email.smtp_from_name`/
`smtp_from_address`. `None` (default) falls back to that same
deployment-wide address -- this section reuses `config.email`'s SMTP
transport (host/port/credentials/`enabled`) unconditionally; it never
grows its own SMTP block.

recipient_retention_days.description:
How many days recipient rows remain before old partitions are removed.
`0` disables pruning.

alert_emails.description:
AB10-T2: who hears about a built-in alert firing or resolving, by
email (sent through the job queue and the `email` section's relay).

alert_webhooks.description:
AB10-T2: incoming-webhook URLs (Slack, Teams, any service that takes
`{"text": ...}`) told about a built-in alert firing or resolving.

builtin_store.description:
U4-T1: sample this process's metrics into `ops_metric_sample` every
minute, kept 30 days. Unset: on for Solo (`cache.backend = "memory"`),
off otherwise (several servers use Prometheus).

enable_distributed_tracing.description:
P-observability-completion — the enable switch for an OTLP trace
exporter. `false` (every config file's value today) is byte-identical
to today's tracing_subscriber::fmt()-only behavior: no OTel layer
installed, no listener bound, no span exported anywhere.

NOTE ON CURRENT IMPLEMENTATION STATE (be skeptical of any doc that
claims this is fully wired — verify against `crates/server/src/main.rs`
and this crate's Cargo.toml before trusting it): as of this comment,
this flag and `otlp_endpoint` below are validated at boot (see
`validate()`) and the W3C `traceparent` header is extracted/recorded
on the request span by `attome_server::middleware::trace_context`
(wired into `apply_outer_layers` unconditionally, since it degrades to
a no-op when no `traceparent` header is present — which is every
request today, since nothing yet sends one) — but `main.rs` does NOT
yet install a real `tracing-opentelemetry` layer or ship any span to
`otlp_endpoint`. That exporter wiring, and forwarding `traceparent` on
the two outbound HTTP call sites (`attome_auth::oidc`'s discovery/JWKS
fetch) and into `PlatformJob` enqueue call sites, remain unimplemented
— see DECISIONS.md's P-observability-completion entry for the exact
remaining scope and why it was deferred (unverifiable third-party
crate/version surface in an environment with no Rust toolchain to
compile against).

otlp_endpoint.description:
P-observability-completion — the OTLP collector this deployment's own
exporter would send spans to (Grafana Tempo / Jaeger / the OpenTelemetry
Collector — a per-deployment adoption decision, never a hosted/shared
endpoint per D-002). Required (fail-closed, see `validate()`) whenever
`enable_distributed_tracing = true`; `None` otherwise. Currently
validated but not yet read by any exporter — see
`enable_distributed_tracing`'s doc comment above.

profiler_enabled.description:
attome-profiler: live per-probe call count/avg/min/max dashboard (the
Angular "Profiler" admin page). Default false — byte-identical
behavior (no profiler middleware layer, no Redis writes) until a
deployment opts in, same "dark unless configured" posture as
`metrics_port == 0`.

server_timing.description:
AA1-T5: who gets a `Server-Timing` header splitting each response's
time into middleware, authentication, permissions, database, handler
and outside calls. `dev` (the default): every response, in a debug
environment (`APP_ENV=debug`) only. `admins`: responses to signed-in
administrators. `off`: nobody. Measuring the database phase reads
sqlx's per-statement events, which costs a little on every query
while the header can be sent.

trace_sampling_rate.description:
P-observability-completion — `TraceIdRatioBased` sampler ratio once
`enable_distributed_tracing = true`. Meaningless (and unread) while
that flag is false, same "declared but inert until its gate flips"
shape as most other flag-gated fields in this file.

worker_health_port.description:
P-worker-process-split follow-up (the TODO `crates/server/src/bin/
worker.rs` shipped with) — the dedicated `worker` binary has no HTTP
listener at all today, so a split deployment's compose/k8s healthcheck
can only prove the process exists (`pgrep`), not that it can actually
reach Postgres/Redis. Unlike `metrics_port` (dark by default: every
existing config has it at 0), this defaults **on** — a worker
readiness probe should exist out of the box, not require every
deployment to opt in. `0` still disables it, same "0 = off" convention
as `metrics_port`, for a bare-metal/host-networking deployment that
genuinely wants it off. Read by `crates/server/src/bin/worker.rs`
only — `main.rs` never binds this (its own `/health/ready` already
covers the inline-worker case via `app.port`).

client_secret.description:
`${VAR}`-expanded like every other secret in this file (D-038) — never
commit a real value. Length-checked by `AppConfig::validate` same as
`auth.jwt_secret`/`s2s.key_encryption_key`.

display_name.description: Shown on the Angular login page's provider button.

email_claim.description:
ID-token claim carrying the user's email — almost always "email"; a
knob only for a provider with a non-standard claim map.

issuer.description:
Issuer URL, no trailing slash, e.g.
"https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/v2.0" or
"https://accounts.google.com". `{issuer}/.well-known/openid-configuration`
MUST resolve (OIDC discovery, RFC 8414).

mfa_acr_values.description:
Q2-T2: the ID-token `amr` entries or `acr` value that mean the person
passed multi-factor authentication at the provider (a preset's
`mfa_acr_values`, e.g. `["mfa"]` for Entra ID). Empty (the default):
the provider's MFA is never counted.

require_email_verified_claim.description:
Enterprise-audit remediation (Phase 2.2, revised): when `true`, a
missing `email_verified` claim is rejected (`Unauthorized`) instead
of defaulting to accepted. **On by default** — an omitted
`email_verified` claim is indistinguishable at the protocol level
from an IdP that never verifies email at all, so defaulting to
"accept" fails open on exactly the ambiguity this flag exists to
close. A provider whose IdP is confirmed to reliably omit the claim
while still being fully trustworthy (`verify_claims`'s original
reasoning) must opt back out explicitly
(`"require_email_verified_claim": false`) rather than relying on a
silent default.

trust_idp_mfa.description:
Q2-T2: whether MFA the provider reports counts as MFA in Attome, so a
policy that requires MFA is met without Attome's own factor. Set
`false` for a provider whose MFA claim is not trusted.

providers.description:
Keyed by an operator-chosen provider key (e.g. "entra", "okta",
"keycloak", "google") — becomes the `{provider}` path segment in
`/api/v1/auth/oidc/{provider}/login|callback` and the `provider_key`
stored in `xrm_core_user_identity`. Empty (the default) means no OIDC
provider is configured — those routes 404 for any key looked up here.

drill_public_keys.description: Public keys (base64) a drill report's signature is checked against.

drill_signing_key_path.description: The private key that signs recovery-drill reports.

patroni_api_urls.description:
