The Patroni REST API of each database node (`http://db1:8008`), for
cluster status and switchover. Empty: no Patroni cluster.

cursor_default.description:
`true` (default): `query/execute` requests with neither `after_id`
nor `include_total: true` run in keyset/cursor mode from the start of
the result set, instead of OFFSET. Set `false` to restore the pre-P-
stored-query-containment default (plain OFFSET, no total) for one
release as a rollback switch (§7 of the plan) — `include_total: true`
always gets `COUNT(*) OVER()` totals regardless of this flag.

max_offset_rows.description:
AA4-T3: the deepest row an offset page may start at. OFFSET reads and
throws away every row before it, so a deep page costs as much as
reading them all; past this a request is refused with a pointer to
`after_id` (keyset paging), which costs the same at any depth.

timeouts_ms.description:
AA4-T7: how long a query may run, by kind of request. A query past
its limit answers `504 query_timeout` with a hint to run it as an
export.

trigram_index_min_rows.description:
AA4-T5: a filterable text attribute gets a trigram (GIN) index, so a
`contains` filter is index-backed, once its table's estimated row
count reaches this. At least 1; default 100,000.

validate_on_execute.description:
Phase 2's rollback switch: `query/execute` skips the per-request
`EXPLAIN` cost check by default, trusting the cost estimate captured
once in `xrm_core_sql_query_version` at publish time. `true` restores the
pre-phase-2 behavior of re-running `EXPLAIN` on every execute call
(defense against runtime plan drift the cached estimate can't see) —
a kill switch, not a recommended steady-state setting.

QueryTimeouts.description: AA4-T7: statement time limits in milliseconds, by kind of request.

interactive.description: A person waiting on a list or a view (default 500).

report.description: A stored query flagged as a report (default 5000).

RateLimitCategoryLimits.description:
Independent anonymous/authenticated budgets for one rate-limit category
(P-rate-limit-atomicity §4.3). A category absent from `categories` falls
back to `RateLimitSection`'s own top-level `anonymous_rpm`/
`authenticated_rpm` — an upgrading deployment that never touches this
block is unaffected except for the categories this plan deliberately
tightens (credential/mfa/password_reset ship a lower default than the
blanket `api` number).

categories.description:
P-rate-limit-atomicity: keyed by category name (`credential`, `mfa`,
`password_reset`, `api`, `export`, `expensive_query`, ...), resolved
against `attome_server::middleware::rate_limit::RATE_LIMIT_CATEGORIES`'
compile-time (method, route-template) → category table. Replaces the
old `per_endpoint_limits` map outright — that map only ever changed
which number was checked against one shared identity-only bucket, it
never isolated a per-endpoint budget the way its name implied (see
D-145). A deployment with a leftover `per_endpoint_limits` key fails
to boot (below) rather than silently losing an override it believes
still applies.

ipv6_bucket_prefix.description:
BSV-F16 (B6) — both per-IP limiters bucket an IPv6 client by this
prefix length rather than its full /128, because one host usually
controls a whole /64 and could otherwise rotate addresses inside it to
dodge the limit. IPv4 is always bucketed per address. Range 32..=128;
128 restores per-address buckets.

pre_auth_rpm.description:
Coarse, IP-only limit applied by `pre_auth_rate_limit` — the layer that
runs before `s2s_authn`/`authn` so a flood of garbage JWTs/HMAC
signatures gets rejected before burning crypto + a Redis
denylist/nonce lookup per request. Deliberately looser than
`anonymous_rpm` (a blunt pre-crypto backstop, not a business-logic
limit) — an unmeasured starting guess; tune against real traffic once
available.

host.description:
P-ha-failover-hardening follow-up / D-155 — closes the gap D-125
flagged ("`ReadonlyDbCredentials` only overrides user/password, there
is no host/port override for the readonly role"): lets the readonly
pool point at a genuinely different endpoint than
`database.host`/`.port` — e.g. a Patroni HAProxy replica-routing
listener (`deploy/ha/haproxy.cfg`'s `postgres_replicas`, port 5433)
or a pgbouncer `attome_ro` alias on its own port. `None` (the
default) falls back to `database.host` — today's behavior, unchanged.
Unlike `readonly` itself (required outside debug, D-038), leaving
this unset is never a boot error: a deployment sharing one endpoint
for both roles (today's default topology) is still fully supported.

port.description:
See `host` above — same override, for the port. `None` falls back to
`database.port`.

notify_roles.description:
Who the post-apply notification goes to. Unset (the default) keeps
today's recipients: the active holders of the admin privilege. Set,
the notification goes to the active holders of these roles (by role
`name`) instead; the recipient cap is unchanged. When none of the
named roles has an active holder the notification falls back to the
admin holders (logged at `warn`), so a stale name never silences it.
A set list must be non-empty, without blanks or duplicates, at most
[`MAX_NOTIFY_ROLES`] names (a boot error otherwise).

allowed_regions.description: The regions data may live in; empty for no rule.

components.description: A component's region, overriding what its configuration declares.

RetentionSection.description:
P-retention-archive-completion §3a — policy-driven partition archive/drop,
entity-record purge, and legal hold. Config-driven per D-002's
single-deployment-per-customer model: every field below is one
deployment's own `config.json`, never a cross-customer policy table.

Every window defaults to `None` ("keep forever") and `dry_run` defaults
`true`, so a fresh deployment with no `retention` block behaves exactly as
today — zero automatic archive/drop/purge behavior until an operator
explicitly configures a window **and** flips `dry_run` off **and**
approves a specific proposed action (§3a/§3d/§3e; two independent gates,
neither sufficient alone).

audit_days.description:
Age (in days) past which a `xrm_audit_header`/`xrm_audit_detail`/
`xrm_audit_snapshot` partition becomes archive/drop-eligible.
`None` (default) = keep forever, today's behavior.

disposition_action.description:
M23 Records Management (D-456) — which disposition outcome the daily
sweep proposes for a record past `entity_purge_grace_days`:
`"purge"` (default — today's behavior, crypto-shred + field-scrub, no
evidence kept) or `"archive"` (export to `attome-storage` first,
evidence kept in `xrm_core_archive_record`, then the same
field-scrub — see `xrm_compliance::archive::execute_entity_archive`).
Deployment-wide, same D-002 single-deployment-per-customer convention
as every other field in this section — not a per-record or
per-entity policy table. An unrecognized value falls back to
`"purge"` with a warning rather than failing the sweep (see
`xrm_entity::purge::propose_purge_actions`), the same fail-safe
posture `dry_run`'s default takes.

dry_run.description:
Safety default. While `true` (the default), the propose step always
runs and always writes `xrm_audit_retention_action` rows so an operator can
see exactly what a live run *would* do, but approve/execute are
refused outright with a message naming this flag. Must be explicitly
flipped to `false` before any partition can be dropped or any record
purged.

entity_purge_grace_days.description:
How long (in days) a provisioned entity record may sit
`is_active = false` before it becomes purge-eligible (crypto-shred +
field-scrub, never a hard `DELETE` — see `xrm_entity::purge`).
`None` (default) disables entity purge entirely.

legal_hold.description:
Deployment-wide kill switch (D-002: a litigation hold on a
self-hosted, one-customer-per-deployment platform is realistically an
all-or-nothing freeze for that deployment, not a per-record flag).
While `true`, no archive/drop/purge action may execute regardless of
how far past its window a partition or record is — proposals still
compute, for visibility, but approve/execute are refused outright.

propose_interval_secs.description:
How often the daily proposal sweep re-checks (enqueues
`PlatformJob::ProposeRetentionActions`), in seconds. Idempotent
either way — a shorter interval only means more no-op re-checks once
caught up, never duplicate proposals (migration 0067's partial unique
index makes the insert idempotent).

s2s_access_log_days.description:
Age (in days) past which a `xrm_s2s_access_log` partition becomes
archive/drop-eligible. `None` (default) = keep forever.

RuntimeDbCredentials.description:
P-db-privilege-separation / D-117 — same shape as `ReadonlyDbCredentials`,
for the DML-only `attome_runtime` role.

access_log_enabled.description: Write every S2S request to xrm_s2s_access_log. Default: true.

enabled.description: Enable S2S HMAC authentication. When false the middleware is a no-op.

failure_alert_threshold.description:
Number of 401 failures from one client in 5 minutes that triggers
the admin failure alert. Default: 100.

key_encryption_key.description:
64-hex-char AES-256 master key(s) used to encrypt HMAC secrets at
rest. Required when enabled = true. Generate with: openssl rand -hex 32.
P-key-rotation-and-jwt (a): a `KeyRing` — see that type's doc.

seeded_clients.description:
D-771: S2S clients declared here are reconciled at every boot (client,
one key with a fixed `public_id`, permission rows), so a machine
caller's credential survives a database reset and is rotated by
editing `.env`. Empty by default.

S2sSeededClient.description:
One config-declared S2S client (D-771). `secret` is a `${VAR}` reference;
blank or unresolved means "not configured here" and the client is skipped.

permissions.description: Entity ceiling rows (D-766); empty leaves the client unbounded.

public_id.description: Stable key id the caller sends; must start with `s2s_`.

service_user_email.description: The existing system user the client acts as. Never created here.

csp_enforce.description:
P-frontend-hardening §4(d)/step 7 — report-only kill switch for the
response `Content-Security-Policy` header, mirroring `csrf_enforce`'s
pattern above. `true` (default) sends a real, enforcing
`Content-Security-Policy`; `false` sends
`Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` instead (observe violations,
block nothing) — the plan's own rollout guidance is to set this
`false` as the *first* step in any real deployment, watch for
violations during a burn-in period, then flip it on, precisely
because (unlike `csrf_enforce`, which is safely additive against
existing behavior) there was no prior CSP at all for this to be
layered on top of. See `attome_server::middleware::security_headers`
for the header value itself.

csrf_enforce.description:
P-cookie-csrf-hardening kill switch for the Origin/Fetch-Metadata CSRF
middleware (`attome_server::middleware::csrf`). Default true — the check
only ever rejects a *cookie-authenticated* unsafe-method (POST/PUT/
PATCH/DELETE) request whose `Sec-Fetch-Site`/`Origin` don't match this
deployment, so "on" is the safe default; S2S/ApiKey/no-cookie traffic
is unaffected either way. Set false only to diagnose a reverse proxy
that strips `Origin`/`Sec-Fetch-*` headers — false is log-only
(rejections are `tracing::warn!`'d but the request still proceeds),
never a silent bypass; remove the flag once burned in, never leave it
off in a real deployment.

external_effects_enabled.description:
I-7's deployment-wide air-gap switch: whether any `Effect::External`
capability (`xrm-ai`'s `GateInputs::external_effects_enabled`) is
allowed to reach outside this deployment at all. Default **false** —
an air-gapped or freshly-provisioned deployment refuses every
external-effect action until an operator opts in explicitly, the
same fail-safe-closed posture every other toggle in this section
documents.

Before this field existed, every one of `xrm-ai`'s three call
sites (`engine.rs::gate_inputs`, `server::omnichannel`,
`xrm-workflow::scheduler`) hardcoded `external_effects_enabled:
false` with a comment noting no `Effect::External` action existed
yet to make the gap visible — verified live 2026-09-09, grepping
every call site in the workspace. This field is what those three now
read instead of the literal `false`, and it is also the flag
`trd-engine`'s execution pipeline reads directly (see that crate's
`broker_submitter.rs`) to decide whether the router/adapter stage
may submit a real broker order — **not** through
`xrm_ai::dispatch`, because that path's `Initiator` is `User`/
`Agent` only (I-3) and a LIVE strategy's automated order is neither
(`document/TRADING-PLATFORM-PLAN.md` §6 rule 5, `Initiator::System`).
Reusing this one config flag for both, rather than inventing a
second air-gap switch, is what makes "I-7's deployment flag gates
whether any external routing is enabled at all" (plan Phase 4) an
honest sentence.

hsts_include_subdomains.description:
Appends `; includeSubDomains` to the header above.

Defaults to **false**, unlike every other security toggle in this
section, and deliberately so: HSTS is cached by the browser for the
full `max-age`, so switching this on while any sibling subdomain is
still served over plain http makes that subdomain unreachable for up
to a year, with no server-side way to undo it. Turn it on once every
subdomain of the deployment's origin is confirmed TLS-only — that is
the stronger posture and the recommended end state, just not a safe
thing to inherit silently from a default.

`preload` is deliberately not offered as a toggle: submitting to the
browser preload list is an out-of-band, effectively irreversible
action that must not be reachable by editing a config file.

hsts_max_age_secs.description:
`max-age` (seconds) for the response `Strict-Transport-Security`
header; `0` omits the header entirely. Default one year.

Audit finding: HSTS previously appeared nowhere in `crates/` or
`deploy/`. The assumption was that the separate TLS-edge nginx (D-099
— the one repo that stays outside this monorepo) set it, but nothing
in audited scope pinned or tested that, which made it a control with
no owner. Setting it here gives it one: this process emits it on
every response it serves, exactly the way it already emits CSP, and
`deploy/frontend/nginx.conf` emits the matching header for the static
SPA responses this process never touches.

Safe to leave on in local dev: RFC 6797 §8.1 requires a user agent to
**ignore** an HSTS header received over a non-secure transport, so the
plain-http `:7865` dev server is unaffected.

secret_max_age_days.description:
Z1-T8: days a secret's active key may stay in use before
administrators are reminded (once a day at most, and then once every
30 days per secret) to rotate it. `0` turns the reminder off; the
inventory (`GET /api/v1/admin/secrets`) still shows every age.

strict_privileged_authz.description:
P-authz-revocation-epoch (D-116): always-on synchronous epoch
re-check (fail-closed, `redis_coordination`, 300ms timeout) ahead of
the privileged/admin-gated route bundles (`admin`, `license_admin`,
`s2s_admin`, `schema`, `sidebar`, plus xrm-security's own grant/revoke
admin routes) — a just-revoked admin cannot keep using a still-live
L1 cache entry to perform further privileged operations for the rest
of the ordinary 60s TTL. Default true; false is the emergency
rollback to pre-epoch behavior for exactly those bundles (kill
switch — remove after one release of burn-in per the plan's rollout
section).

strict_revocation.description:
P-record-level-security item (b), implemented as a mode of this same
epoch mechanism rather than a second implementation: when true, EVERY
`SecurityContext` resolve — not just the privileged-bundle class
above — pays the fail-closed epoch re-check, so even an ordinary CRUD
request sees a revoked grant on its very next request instead of
within the 60s TTL. Enabled by default for the enterprise security
posture; development deployments may explicitly set it false when the
per-request Redis round trip is unsuitable.

trusted_proxy_cidrs.description:
The only TCP peers allowed to supply a client address through
`X-Forwarded-For`. Leave empty for direct deployments: forwarding
headers are then ignored and the socket peer is used for rate limiting
and audit IPs. Entries must be IPv4/IPv6 CIDRs, for example
`"172.20.0.0/16"` or `"fd00:dead:beef::/64"`. An IPv4-mapped IPv6 peer
(a dual-stack bind) is matched as its IPv4 address.

BSV-F18 (B7) — the proxies listed here **must** overwrite what the
client sent: nginx `proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For
$proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;` (appends the real peer, which is the hop
this crate trusts, walking from the last header line) and
`proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Host $host;` (replaces any client value;
the last line wins). A trusted proxy is also the only peer whose
inbound `traceparent` becomes the request's trace parent (BSV-D10), so
the edge should strip or set that header too.

endpoint.description: Overrides `https://api.sendgrid.com` (the EU region, a test double).

Overrides `https://email.{region}.amazonaws.com` (a VPC endpoint, a
test double).

interactive_high_water.description:
Interactive requests in flight above which the other classes shrink
to one at a time.

SpendSection.description:
N24-T1 — what generation may cost per rolling month (30 days), in the
unit the prices are written in (the deployment's currency).

Every cap is optional and applies only when the generation model has a
price: a model with no price is never counted against a money budget
(the token budgets still apply). Each cap is a separate window: the
whole deployment, each person (`caller_monthly`), each agent
(`agent_monthly`, for sessions started with an agent) and each feature
(`feature_monthly`, by action id such as `record.summarize`, or
`agent.turn` for chat and agent turns). Once any window passes
`degrade_at_percent` of its cap, generations are shortened to
`degraded_max_output_tokens`; at the cap they are refused (429) before
anything is spent.

degrade_at_percent.description: Percent of a cap at which generations are shortened.

degraded_max_output_tokens.description: The output ceiling near a cap; unset leaves generations unshortened.

prices.description: Price per million tokens, by model id (`inference.generation.model`).

StatementClassOverrides.description: Z2-T5: `database.statement_classes`, one optional override per class.

StatementClassTimeouts.description:
Z2-T5: one statement class's timeouts in milliseconds; each must be
above 0.

StorageBackend.description:
Z6-T1: which object store holds this deployment's files. Every backend
goes through the `object_store` crate, so engines see one `ObjectStore`
whatever is behind it.

oneOf.description:
An S3-compatible bucket (AWS S3, RustFS, MinIO): the `s3_*` settings.
The default.

A folder on this machine: `storage.local`. One node only, since other
nodes cannot see the folder. Browsers upload and download through the
server's own signed `/api/v1/storage/local/` route instead of
presigned bucket URLs.

backend.description:
`s3` (the default), `local`, `azure` or `gcs`. Only the chosen
backend's settings are used; the `s3_*` settings may be left out for
the others.

clamd_address.description:
`host:port` of a ClamAV `clamd` daemon (INSTREAM protocol) the async
scan job submits uploaded bytes to. Empty (the default) means no
scanner is configured — the scan job then fails closed (rejects,
never promotes) rather than silently skipping malware scanning.

encrypt_client_side.description:
Z6-T4: encrypt files in the server on S3, Azure or GCS too, instead of
relying on the backend's own server-side encryption. Needs
`encryption_key`. Presigned download links then serve ciphertext, so
leave it off unless downloads go through the server.

encryption_key.description:
Z6-T4: the key-encryption-key ring files are encrypted under, its own
trust domain (D-069). Each file gets its own data key, wrapped by this
ring's active key and stored in the file's header. Set, it encrypts
every file on `local` storage, and on the other backends when
`encrypt_client_side` is true; empty (the default), nothing is
encrypted by the server. Every entry is 64 hex chars (a boot error
otherwise). Keep old keys in the ring after a rotation: files sealed
under them still name them.

max_deployment_storage_bytes.description:
Soft cap on the whole deployment's promoted (`clean`) file storage —
meaningful because D-099's data-plane model is one dedicated
deployment per customer, so this is that customer's total quota, not
a cross-customer figure. `None` (the default) disables the check,
same reasoning and TODO as `max_user_storage_bytes` above.

max_entity_storage_bytes.description:
Z6-T7: caps on the files of one entity's records, by the entity's
logical name (`{"contract": 10737418240}`), counted like the user cap.
An entity not named has no cap of its own; the user and deployment
caps still apply. Empty (the default) sets none.

max_upload_size_bytes.description:
Max `declared_size_bytes` an upload session may declare; enforced at
finalize (HEAD-verified against what was actually PUT), not at
presign time (§4.2's documented limitation).

TODO(item 26): true presign-time enforcement — S3 itself refusing an
oversized PUT before it ever lands in quarantine storage — is still
not possible with this crate. Confirmed against `object_store` 0.14's
`Signer` trait (`attome-storage/src/presign.rs`): `signed_url(method,
path, expires_in)` takes no content-length/policy constraint, so
there is no signed header or condition this code can attach to the
presigned PUT URL to make S3/RustFS reject a too-large body itself.
Closing this fully needs an architecture change — either switching
upload sessions to presigned POST-policy uploads (S3's
`content-length-range` condition), which changes the client contract
(`create_upload_session`'s response shape and the Angular
`file-upload.service.ts` PUT flow both), or a storage client that
exposes SigV4 signed-header control — not attempted here per
guidelines' scope-discipline ("implement a safe containment... report
the remaining work"). What *is* implemented as containment: the
`max_user_storage_bytes`/`max_deployment_storage_bytes` quotas below
bound how much quarantine exposure one user (or the deployment as a
whole) can accumulate before finalize/orphan-sweep clears it, and the
`presign` rate-limit category
(`attome-server/middleware/rate_limit.rs`) bounds how fast a single
caller can mint new quarantine capacity.

max_user_storage_bytes.description:
Soft cap on one user's total upload-session footprint: the sum of
`declared_max_size_bytes` across their non-terminal sessions
(`pending`/`uploaded`/`scanning`) plus `actual_size_bytes` across
their `clean` ones. Checked in `create_upload_session` before a new
session is created (item 26 remediation — a per-user quota). `None`
(the default) disables the check: an unmeasured cap would be a guess,
not evidence (guidelines §14) — TODO(item 26): pick a real number
with the ops/customer team once there is usage data, then set this in
each deployment's `config.json`.

quota_warning_pct.description:
Z6-T7: the share of a cap, in percent, past which administrators are
told (once a day per cap). 80 by default.

s3_public_endpoint.description:
Endpoint embedded in presigned upload/download URLs, which browsers
(or any other client) request directly. SigV4 signs the `Host`, so the
URL must be signed for the address the client will actually contact;
a proxy rewriting the host afterwards invalidates the signature.

When set, it must be reachable by those clients, serve this same
`s3_bucket`, route path-style `/{bucket}/{key}` requests with path and
query preserved, and accept the `Host` it was signed for. It never
replaces `s3_endpoint`: server-side reads and writes always use
`s3_endpoint`. Empty (the default) signs presigned URLs for
`s3_endpoint`, which is right whenever that address is already
client-reachable (e.g. AWS S3 proper).

s3_verify_ssl.description:
Whether HTTPS certificates from the S3 endpoints are verified. It does
not choose the transport: the endpoint's scheme does (`http://` is
plaintext whatever this says; `https://`, or empty for AWS S3, is TLS).
`false` accepts any certificate on a TLS endpoint. Production refuses
`false`.

TlsSection.description:
Z5-T6: `app.tls`. Off by default: the server speaks plain HTTP, as behind
a TLS-terminating proxy.

cert_path.description: The PEM certificate chain, leaf first.

enabled.description: Serve HTTPS on `app.port` from the certificate and key below.

key_path.description: The PEM private key (PKCS#8, PKCS#1 or SEC1).

min_version.description: The oldest TLS version accepted: `"1.2"` (the default) or `"1.3"`.

TranslationSection.description:
N20-T1 — how `text.translate` renders the deployment's own terms:
`glossary` maps a term to its translation per language code, e.g.
`{ "Purchase order": { "ar": "أمر شراء" } }`. A term found in the text
is given to the model with its required translation.

max_depth.description:
Default crawl depth when `POST /targets` doesn't specify one — each
crawl can override this per request (clamped to a sane range by the
handler), stored on its own `xrm_webcrawl_target.max_depth` row.

approval.description:
D-195 / P-four-eyes-approval — which `attome_approval` action_type
strings require dual-control approval instead of executing inline.
Empty by default (opt-in, same "ships dark behind a flag" posture as
`idempotency`/`audit.chainer_enabled`) — a deployment names an action
here only once a customer's security policy or compliance framework
actually requires it (the backlog's own trigger condition).

backup.description: U6-T1 — the daily local database backup. On by default.

capability.description:
D-344 (amends D-167) — the durability-capability gate. Governs a
*route-level* 503 for operations that cannot durably complete
(upload, bulk import, mail resend), never node readiness. See
`CapabilitySection`'s doc comment for why `enforcement_enabled`
defaults on where most flags in this tree ship dark.

change_feed.description:
M01 §7 C-04 — how long a change-feed row that every registered
consumer has passed is kept before `PlatformJob::PruneChangeFeed`
deletes it. See `ChangeFeedSection`'s doc comment.

deployment.description:
P-data-protection-governance §4 — data-residency declaration; see
`DeploymentSection`'s doc comment.

docgen.description:
M57 Phase 1 — Document Generation. The isolated render sidecar's
address plus its explicit timeout/size caps. See `DocgenSection`'s
doc comment.

einvoice.description:
AG2 — e-invoicing. Ships dark (`enabled: false`): see
`EinvoiceSection`'s doc comment.

events.description:
M62 Phase 1 — Event Bus subscriptions/webhook delivery. Ships dark
(`webhooks_enabled: false`). See `EventsSection`'s doc comment.

fleet.description:
D-792 — the fleet console (developer machine only). Empty by default;
refused on the production profile. See `FleetSection`'s doc comment.

idempotency.description:
P-idempotency-hardening §4.4/§4.5 — the durable-tier
mandatory-operation policy. Additive/opt-in (empty by default): a
deployment must explicitly name routes here before any request starts
requiring `X-Idempotency-Key`, matching `audit.chainer_enabled`'s
"ships dark behind a flag" precedent. D-327: that "empty by default"
posture is deliberately narrowed under `app.deployment_profile =
"production"` — `server::boot::init`'s `validate_operation_registries`
additionally requires every `xrm_server::bulk::
MANDATORY_TIER_OPERATIONS` entry to be present here before a
production process boots. `attome-config` can't express that floor
itself (zero xrm-* knowledge, guidelines §1), so it isn't part of
`validate_production_profile` below despite living right next to
every other production-only requirement enforced there.

inference.description:
D-360 / P-inference — model endpoints and the AI kill-switch
(TODO-055). Ships dark: every surface defaults off, so a deployment
that upgrades into a build containing AI code gets no AI behaviour and
no model traffic until an operator opts in.

integration.description:
M59 Phase 1 — Integration & Connectors. Ships dark (`enabled: false`):
see `IntegrationSection`'s doc comment.

metadata.description:
Solution 7 Phase 1 (D-785) — how metadata admin writes are recorded
as changesets. See `ChangesetsSection`'s doc comment.

notification.description:
In-app notification inbox lifecycle policy. Kept separate from audit
retention because notification rows have different ownership.

ops.description:
AB4-T1 — the reliability engine's settings (Patroni, recovery drills).
Empty by default. See `OpsSection`'s doc comment.

portal.description:
D-588 — external-audience web portals: the OIDC providers they may
offer and the signup CAPTCHA. See `PortalSection`'s doc comment.

residency.description:
R7-T1 — where data may live and where each component holds it; see
`crate::residency`.

retention.description:
P-retention-archive-completion — partition archive/drop, entity
purge, and legal hold policy. See `RetentionSection`'s doc comment.

shed.description: AB5-T7 — priority load shedding: slots per request class.

webchat.description:
D-558 — the public web-chat assistant (chatbot plan C9). Ships dark
(`enabled: false`), and enabling it requires an agent definition and
both spend caps. See `WebchatSection`'s doc comment.

webcrawl.description:
D-365 — Web Crawling for Knowledge Base. Ships dark (`enabled: false`):
the platform's first feature that makes an outbound HTTP request to an
arbitrary, user-supplied URL. See `WebcrawlSection`'s doc comment.
